metadata.subject: GENERAL SCIENCE - PAPER II (BIOLOGICAL SCIENCE)
metadata.chapter_name: CHAPTER 2 : RESPIRATION - THE ENERGY RELEASING SYSTEM
instructions: Read the question paper carefully during the 15 minutes allotted reading time.
All answers should be written in the answer booklet provided.
The question paper consists of 4 Sections (Section I, II, III and IV).
Internal choice is available in Section IV (Long Answer / Essay Questions).
Draw neat, well-labeled diagrams wherever necessary.

sections.title: SECTION - I
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL the questions. Each question carries 1 Mark.

questions.question: What is the role of the epiglottis during the process of swallowing food and breathing?
Why does a person feel muscle fatigue and severe cramps after vigorous physical exercise?
Which of the following represents the correct respiratory organ in Earthworm and Cockroach respectively?
In the experiment demonstrating anaerobic respiration in yeast, why is liquid paraffin wax poured over the glucose solution?
options: A) To supply additional nutrients to yeast
B) To prevent atmospheric oxygen from entering the solution
C) To absorb carbon dioxide gas

questions.question: Identify the indicator dye (Janus Green B / Diazine Green) used to test the absence of oxygen in anaerobic respiration experiments. What color change indicates absence of oxygen?
Name the tiny grape-like structural and functional units of the human lungs where gaseous exchange takes place.

sections.title: SECTION - II
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL questions in 3-4 sentences each. Each question carries 2 Marks.

questions.question: Write the correct chronological pathway of air movement in human respiratory system from nostrils to cellular level.
Differentiate between Aerobic Respiration and Anaerobic Respiration based on end products and energy released (number of ATP molecules).
Plants respire through stomata on leaves. What specialized structures do woody stems and mangrove aerial roots use for gaseous exchange?
Why is ATP often referred to as the 'Universal Energy Currency' of the cell? How much energy is stored in one ATP molecule?

sections.title: SECTION - III
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL questions in 5-6 sentences each. Each question carries 4 Marks.

questions.heading: Analyze the given table showing the percentage composition of gases in Inhaled Air and Exhaled Air, then answer the following questions:
sub_questions: i) Why does the percentage of Oxygen decrease from 21% to 16% in exhaled air?
ii) Why does Carbon dioxide show a dramatic increase from 0.04% to 4.4%?
iii) Why does the percentage of Nitrogen remain unchanged (78%) in both inhaled and exhaled air?
iv) What is the biological significance of exhaled air containing higher moisture and heat?

questions.question: Tabulate four clear differences between Respiration (biological oxidation) and Combustion (burning of sugar).

Draw a neat, well-labeled diagram of a single Mitochondrion ('Powerhouse of the Cell'). Label the following parts:
i) Outer membrane  ii) Inner membrane  iii) Cristae  iv) Matrix.
Describe how gaseous exchange takes place across the alveolar membrane into pulmonary blood capillaries by simple diffusion.

sections.title: SECTION - IV
sections.instruction: Note: Answer ALL questions. Each question carries 8 Marks. There is an INTERNAL CHOICE (A or B) for each question.

choice_a.title: A) Explain an experiment to demonstrate the evolution of Carbon Dioxide (CO2) during Anaerobic Respiration (Fermentation) in yeast.
choice_a.format:
Write your answer under the following headings:
• Aim of the Experiment
• Apparatus & Materials Required
• Experimental Procedure (including role of liquid paraffin wax and diazine green)
• Observations (Lime water test result)
• Precautions to be taken

choice_b.title: B) Describe an experiment to prove that Heat is liberated during cellular respiration using germinating seeds.
choice_b.format:
Write your answer under the following headings:
• Aim
• Apparatus Required (Thermos flasks, Thermometer, Cotton wool, Germinating seeds vs Boiled seeds)
• Step-by-step Procedure
• Observations recorded at regular intervals
• Conclusion & Precautions

choice_a.title: A) Draw a neat and labeled diagram of the Human Respiratory System.
sub_tasks: Label the following parts: Larynx, Trachea, Bronchi, Lungs, Alveoli, and Diaphragm.
Explain the mechanism of Breathing (Inspiration and Expiration) with the role of the Diaphragm and Intercostal muscles.

choice_b.title: B) Explain the complete biochemical stages of Cellular Respiration in eukaryotic organisms.
sub_tasks: Describe the three main stages: Glycolysis (in cytoplasm), Krebs Cycle (in mitochondrial matrix), and Electron Transport System (in cristae).
Provide the overall balanced chemical equation of aerobic respiration and calculate the total net gain of ATP molecules produced per molecule of glucose oxidized.
